questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: What fabric protects a motorcycle rider the most?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for riders.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. Pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should motorcycle riders watch for?

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking spot.

questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked cars. Drivers may suddenly leave parking spaces or pull away from the curb.

questions.question: What should you do if a driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the side and let them share your lane.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider improve their visibility?
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials. Always use your headlight, and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: You don't need to check the tire pressure.
It will handle the same as your own bike.
The owner will make sure the brakes work.
Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to react faster.
questions.explanation: Check the borrowed motorcycle the same way you check your own. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar bike and keep extra stopping distance.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road hazards ahead.

questions.question: What does space between your motorcycle and other vehicles do?

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Keeps you in one spot in your lane with less room to move.
Lets you depend on others to find hazards.
Requires you to go faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of having an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend in with traffic so other drivers do not notice you.
Do not use turn signals unless you are riding at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Stay very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Let them know what you plan to do by using your turn signals and brake light. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Look ahead about 12 seconds and be ready to react to any dangers.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is safer than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle can pass if the pass is done before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride faster to get away from them.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Riding faster may make it worse by causing them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: The body gets rid of one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: To find how much alcohol remains, subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals about four drinks still in the body.

questions.question: Which color is best to wear so others can see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding. Bright clothing makes you easier to see at any time of day.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: One brake or the other, but never both together.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time. They work best when used together.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers do not lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to gain distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If possible, change lanes and let the tailgater pass you. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects:

options.text: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make riding unsafe. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see other vehicles' lights better.
Harder than riding during the day because you cannot see as well.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than riding during the day because you cannot see as well.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because visibility is poor. It is harder to see and be seen. Without natural light and shadows, it is difficult to judge distances correctly.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not provide proper protection.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still remain in your body.
You will be safe as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain in your body.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system. Even waiting can leave you impaired. Your ability to ride safely and think clearly can still be affected.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only during the day.

questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps you be seen at all times. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wearing bright clothing day and night is important for your safety.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of having an accident, you should:

options.text: Ride within one foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Signal only when you feel like it.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and correct lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides of your bike.
